title: Redwood discovery with Lumen Finance - cost/unit economics
next_steps: Redwood to send per-token pricing tiers and sample calculator
Customer to share sample query distribution + monthly token estimates
Schedule technical deep dive and benchmarking week-of Aug 25
action_items: Maya: Send pricing sheet and batching/caching guide by 2025-08-17
Carlos: Prep benchmark plan and request list by 2025-08-18
Anita: Share anonymized token usage histogram and latency SLOs by 2025-08-20
summary: Initial discovery focused on per-token economics, batching and caching levers, and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments for Lumen's inference workloads.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya from redwood, im the AE on the account. quick roll call?  
[00:06] Anita Desai: Anita here, head of ML at Lumen Finance.  
[00:10] Rahul Mehra: Rahul infra, hey. Jason on shortly.  
[00:15] Carlos Ruiz: Carlos, solutions engineer here at Redwood. we'll dig into perf and economics today.  
[00:22] Maya: Great. goal is to understand your current stack, token volumes, latency requirements and budget so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private.  
[00:31] Anita: Yep, high level — we're running customer-facing assistants for financial planning, mix of short prompts and long contexts. currently doing in-house with a combination of GPUs and OpenAI API for spikes. costs are creeping up.  
[00:45] Maya: Understood. can you ballpark current token/month and percent of real-time vs batch?  
[00:52] Anita: rough — 200M tokens/month, 70% real-time chat, 30% batch night jobs. latency target for chat is 400-600ms p95. budget is... we're trying to keep inference under $20k/month to start.  
[01:12] Carlos: ok that's helpful. so two levers: per-token pricing (hosted) and per-hour reserved capacity (dedicated) plus batching/caching to reduce tokens. for 200M tokens hosted could be expensive depending on model choice.  
[01:29] Rahul: can you explain how batching and kv cache concretely reduce cost? we have lots of repeated prefixes and system prompts.  
[01:36] Carlos: sure — batching bundles requests together on the GPU, amortizing compute overhead so effective cost/token drops. KV caching is prefix/kv cache — if you have repeated conversation history or repeated system prompts, we can avoid recomputing early layers and reuse key-value cache which saves tokens and compute. both reduce unit cost; caching helps latency too if cache hits are local.  
[01:54] Anita: how often do cache hits occur in practice? our prompts vary a lot but system prompts are same.  
[02:02] Carlos: depends — system prompt cache hits are near 100% for same prompt, for user history it depends on overlap. we typically see 10-30% effective token savings from cache plus another 20-40% from batching depending on workload shape.  
[02:16] Maya: important tradeoff is hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved capacity. with hosted you pay per token; with dedicated you commit to GPUs which gives lower per-token compute but you pay for idle capacity.  
[02:30] Jason Cole: if we move to dedicated what are typical savings? and how does quantization help?  
[02:36] Carlos: dedicated can reduce unit cost 30-60% depending on utilization. quantization (int8/int4) reduces GPU memory and inference time — yields another 10-30% cost improvement.  
[02:47] Rahul: our traffic spikes a lot — how do autoscaling and burst capacity work?  
[02:53] Maya: dedicated supports burst pools and autoscaling policies; you can set reserved baseline and allow bursts to hosted capacity, or buy burst credits. that helps avoid over-provisioning for peak.  
[03:04] Anita: security — we need SOC2, KMS, VPC peering, and audit logs. is that available?  
[03:10] Maya: yes. Hosted has SOC2 and enterprise plans support KMS integration and VPC peering via Redwood Private — Private is the model for fully customer-controlled network and on-prem.  
[03:20] Carlos: note that Private adds ops overhead and licensing; cost model is typically platform fee plus infra.  
[03:26] Anita: ok. for our budget of $20k/month, what path makes sense to get started?  
[03:33] Carlos: usually start hosted for quick time-to-value, then move to dedicated once you pass a utilization threshold — we can model break-even: for your 200M tokens, with moderate batching/caching, dedicated may break even around 150-250M tokens depending on model and quantization.  
[03:50] Maya: we'll send a cost calculator. can you share token distribution per prompt length?  
[03:56] Anita: yes we'll pull histograms.  
[04:00] Rahul: any competitor gaps we should watch for?  
[04:03] Maya: folks mention OpenAI or Anthropic for easy hosted API; VMware/ internal infra for control. Redwood's differentiation is unified runtime + clear optimization levers and predictable pricing for dedicated.  
[04:16] Jason: curious about pricing tiers and sample numbers — per-token for hosted, per-gpu-hour for dedicated?  
[04:22] Maya: right — hosted: per-inference token charges (input+output), tiered by model. dedicated: monthly GPU commit + optional usage overage at lower unit cost. we'll include sample math for your mix.  
[04:36] Carlos: small demo of batching effect — (screen noise) ... so if you send 50 concurrent small requests batching each 32 requests we save around 35% CPU time on that model.  
[04:55] Anita: can you run a pilot? we'd like to benchmark with our prompts and target latency constraints.  
[05:01] Maya: yes, pilot is typical — we can do a 2-week benchmark on Redwood hosted/dedicated staging. will need sample prompts and acceptance criteria.  
[05:10] Rahul: what's realistic SLO we can expect for 400ms p95?  
[05:14] Carlos: with dedicated and quantized model we can hit 300-500ms p95 for small to medium models, depends on sequence length. hosted can hit similar but depends on tenant load and routing; dedicated is more predictable.  
[05:29] Anita: what do you need for the pilot?  
[05:33] Maya: sample prompt set, target models, sample volumes, and a PO to cover reserved capacity if we choose dedicated pilot. else hosted trial credits can work for hosted benchmark.  
[05:44] Jason: who owns pricing negotiation?  
[05:47] Maya: I'll handle AE-side pricing and discounts; SE (Carlos) will own benchmark configs.  
[05:53] Maya: ok let's recap next steps.  
[05:55] Carlos: Action items ...  
[05:57] (cross talk)  
[06:00] Maya: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the pricing sheet and scheduler.  
[06:05] Anita: thanks, bye.
